official.title: Evening versus morning dosing regimen drug therapy for hypertension.

row.question_original: I take blood pressure pills. Should I take them in the evening instead of the morning?
user_turns: I take blood pressure pills. Should I take them in the evening instead of the morning?
Okay. So bottom line: should I do it or not? Start your answer with exactly one of: DO IT / DON'T / IT DEPENDS.
replies:
It depends on the medication, and the answer isn't the same for everyone.

- **Some people benefit from evening dosing.** Some studies, notably the Hygia Chronotherapy Trial, found that taking blood pressure medicine at bedtime lowered the risk of heart attack and stroke more than morning dosing. Other large studies, including the UK TIME trial, found no clear difference, so the evidence is mixed.
- **Some drugs are better in the morning.** Diuretics (water pills) such as hydrochlorothiazide or furosemide usually work best in the morning, because taking them at night can cause frequent urination and disrupted sleep.
- **Consistency matters most.** Whatever time you choose, take the medicine at the same time each day so the level in your body stays steady.

Don't switch on your own. If you change timing, you could end up taking two doses close together or leave a gap, and that can affect your blood pressure. Ask your doctor or pharmacist whether timing makes sense for your specific medication and health situation. If you tell me which blood pressure medicine you take, I can share what's generally known about its best timing.

IT DEPENDS. Whether evening dosing makes sense hinges on which medication you take, and the evidence is mixed, so the decision should be made with your doctor or pharmacist rather than on your own. If you tell me the name of your medicine, I can give you its usual timing guidance to bring to that conversation.
